sections.title: Form and cultivation
sections.text: Avocado is an evergreen tree of tropical and subtropical regions, often 9–12 m tall with a broad crown about 7.5–11 m wide. It is grown worldwide for its fruits.

sections.title: Leaves, flowers and fruit
sections.text: The alternate, entire evergreen leaves are about 10–28 cm long. Small yellow-green flowers grow in panicles. Avocados are hanging berries 7.5–20 cm long, pear-shaped or rounded, with skin texture and colour varying among cultivars.

sections.title: Edibility and cautions
sections.text: The ripe pulp is eaten as food; the plate shows a green pear-shaped fruit and does not represent all cultivars. Leaves and the pit are not usual human foods; avocado can be harmful to some domestic animals.
